title: Speculative-decoding prune: prevent double-charging when speculative tokens are pruned at finalization
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We introduced speculative decoding (speculative sampling + early token emission) to reduce latency for cold requests. The runtime emits speculative token fragments that may later be pruned or replaced during finalization (e.g., when a higher-probability re-sampled beam replaces earlier speculative tokens). Problem: current metering sometimes charges both the speculative fragments and the final tokens when pruning/merge occurs, producing double-billing on a subset of mid-stream handoffs and pruning events. This ticket formalizes invariants, implements deterministic ledger adjustments at finalization, and instruments end-to-end tests to ensure no customer is billed for speculative tokens that were not included in the final delivered completion.
acceptance_criteria: Speculative tokens emitted to clients but later pruned/rolled-back are not charged to customer invoicing ledgers (no double charges), proven by end-to-end playback tests.
Ledger anchors are produced at fragment emission and finalization; finalization reconciles and retracts speculative credits atomically across the proxy, runtime, and billing services.
Edge case: mid-stream model handoffs (variant fallback) with speculative outputs handled without net additional charge; regression tests for handoff scenarios pass.
Telemetry: dashboard shows zero net speculative double-charge incidents in 14-day synthetic-run after rollout; alerts throttle if > 0.05% of sessions show discrepancies.
Performance: added reconciliation logic does not increase p99 latency for non-speculative sessions by >5% in canary region.
implementation_notes: Design invariants: every speculative fragment must be stamped with a stable provisional_token_range_id at emission that survives proxy hops and is referenced in finalization RPC.
Ledger model: implement provisional credits that can be committed or voided during finalization; provisional credits kept in an append-only provisional table for auditability.
API contract: finalization RPC must include list of provisional_token_range_ids to commit and list to revoke; ids not mentioned within TTL are auto-voided.
Trade-offs: Using provisional table increases write amplification for high-throughput paths; mitigate by batching provisional writes per-session with write-behind flush.
Fallback: if finalization RPC fails, mark session as 'pending-reconciled' and surface to billing-run with highest-priority remediation path to avoid customer-visible overcharge.
plan_steps: 1) Design review with runtime and billing owners (done 2025-01-14) - RFC linked below.
2) Implement provisional_token_range_id propagation in websocket proxy and request router (ENG PR #12876).
3) Add provisional_credit table and commit/void API in billing service; add idempotency tokens for finalization RPCs.
4) Add reconciliation worker that listens for finished sessions and applies commit/void with chained idempotency checks.
5) End-to-end synthetic playback harness covering: simple stream, speculative prune, beam-replace, mid-session handoff, dropped finalization RPC.
6) Canary rollout to region-us-east-1 with 1% traffic, monitor loss-rate and billing discrepancies dashboard.
notes: Initial post-merge verification plan captured in DRIVE: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SpeculativeMetering
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Increased write load on billing DB under heavy speculative traffic. Mitigation: batch provisional writes per-session and TTL-based compaction.

Risk: Loss of provisional_token_range_id during proxy restarts. Mitigation: keep mapping persisted in short-lived session-state store with 30s replication window; finalization accepts best-effort matches and flags mismatches for manual review.
Risk: Canary finds unexplained voids leading to underbilling. Mitigation: require dual-writer shadow logging for 48h to reconcile ledger entries before automatic voiding.
